# codigate_domain (Resource)

A custom domain claimed by the workspace. Publish the TXT record from challenge_name/challenge_value, then set verify = true (or verify in the dashboard). Apps on the domain and its subdomains need it verified.

## Example Usage

```terraform
resource "codigate_domain" "example" {
  name   = "example.com"
  verify = true
}

# Publish the challenge with any DNS provider, for example Cloudflare.
resource "cloudflare_dns_record" "codigate_challenge" {
  zone_id = var.cloudflare_zone_id
  name    = codigate_domain.example.challenge_name
  type    = codigate_domain.example.challenge_type
  content = codigate_domain.example.challenge_value
  ttl     = 300
}
```

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Required

- `name` (String) Domain name, for example example.com. Changing it replaces the domain.

### Optional

- `verify` (Boolean) Check the TXT record on every apply while the domain is unverified. Apply succeeds with a warning when the record is not found yet.

### Read-Only

- `challenge_host` (String) Name of the TXT record relative to the domain.
- `challenge_name` (String) Full name of the TXT record.
- `challenge_type` (String) DNS record type to publish (TXT).
- `challenge_value` (String) Value of the TXT record.
- `expires_at` (String) When an unverified claim is dropped (null once verified).
- `id` (String) Domain id.
- `verified` (Boolean) Whether the domain is verified.
- `verified_at` (String) Verification time (RFC 3339).

## Import

Import is supported using the following syntax:

The [`terraform import` command](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/cli/commands/import) can be used, for example:

```shell
# By id or by name.
terraform import codigate_domain.example example.com
```
